overall: The AG found the Trust violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently detailed April 29 notice (three items) and approving insufficiently detailed minutes, but did not find the violations intentional and ordered compliance and minute amendments.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 29 notice item 'Corner Spot - Cherry Street' was insufficiently detailed because it did not describe the anticipated discussion.
allegations.key_passage: although it provides the location of the property to be discussed, does not provide any information about the anticipated nature of the discussion

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice item 'CHAPA/MHP Meeting – Emergency Assistance' used acronyms the public would not understand.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the acronyms for the Citizens’ Housing and Planning Association and Massachusetts Housing Partnership were too obscure to reasonably inform the public of the Trust’s planned discussion.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice item 'Correspondence with citizen' was too vague because it did not state the topic of the discussion.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the item “Correspondence with citizen” was insufficiently detailed because it does not advise the public of the anticipated issue to be discussed.

allegations.summary: Complaint argued the 'Correspondence with citizen' item should have named the person who sent the correspondence.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to find here that the name of the person who sent the correspondence was necessary nor would have been sufficient in order for the notice to be adequately detailed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the approved minutes of the April 29 meeting were insufficiently detailed, particularly the discussion of how to respond to resident emails.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that this section of the April 29 minutes is insufficiently detailed, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the notice and minutes violations were intentional; the AG considered whether the violations were knowing.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore decline to find the violation regarding the insufficiently detailed meeting notice to be intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Amend the April 29 meeting minutes to add sufficient detail about the discussion of how to respond to town resident correspondence, within 60 days of receipt of the determination
remedy_passage: We order the Trust’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Trust that a subsequent determination by our Office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law. We also order the Trust to amend the minutes of the April 29 meeting to include sufficient detail about the discussion surrounding how to respond to town resident correspondence within 60 days of receipt of this determination.
